scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-SLOW-RESPONSE-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a response-capacity problem in Customer Service, and an AI agent that auto-answers tickets (and auto-corrects bills) would resolve it.

H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI reads from the vendor (ORG-AMI/MDMS) are failing to arrive or validate correctly since August, pushing bills into estimate substitution and causing wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Manual field meter reads from the contracted vendor (ORG-FIELD) became delayed or incomplete since August, increasing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced a defect that mis-processes reads or applies wrong tariffs, directly causing incorrect bills.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-MISCAL.statement: The estimate-substitution logic used when no accepted read is available is itself miscalibrated, producing systematically wrong estimated bills independent of any single upstream handoff failure.

H-ACTUAL-READ-PROCESSING-DEFEC.statement: A defect in billing import/processing or bill issuance (independent of whether the underlying read is ACTUAL or ESTIMATED) is causing wrong bills, explaining why most disputed bills (1785/3025) are on ACTUAL reads.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A field-reader headcount shortfall of three since July is the specific driver of late manual-read routes and the resulting estimate substitution, as claimed by SH-FIELD.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-IMPORT-REJE.statement: Billing import validation rejects legitimate AMI reads flagged as high-consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution for 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, rather than true AMI non-delivery.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Authoritative CRM data confirms the ticket-volume doubling claimed in CL-01: monthly disputes went from ~600 in June/July to ~1180-1260 in August/September, an onset coinciding with August. The record only establishes the symptom's magnitude and timing; it does not identify which process step (AMI, field reads, billing rules, estimate logic, or response capacity) caused it.

CRM response-time data (E-02) shows Customer Service is handling disputes well within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days) across 2440 tickets. This indicates response speed/capacity is not the bottleneck; the surge is a volume problem, not a slow-handling problem.

An authoritative, complete query of billing-db's tariff change log returns zero records, meaning no tariff changes were logged. This rules out tariff changes as a cause of the dispute surge but says nothing about read-processing/import-validation defects or AMI/field read delivery.

E-04 shows disputed bills split by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL, so the majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) are on ACTUAL meter reads, not estimated ones. This means the estimate-substitution pathway (triggered by AMI/field read-delivery failures) can explain at most a minority of disputed bills; something else is causing disputes on bills with normal ACTUAL reads too.

E-04 still shows the raw split of disputed bills by read type (1240 ESTIMATED, 1785 ACTUAL). It no longer supports that the ESTIMATED subset arises from an AMI/field-route delivery-failure-triggered estimate-substitution pathway: E-12 shows 1184/1240 ESTIMATED bills are AMI reads rejected on import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), not field-route-shortfall-driven estimate substitution, contradicting PR-CHAIN-2 and partially contradicting PR-ROOT's secondary-driver framing.

Field route-log data (E-05) shows manual meter-read route completion at 88% against a 95% target for 9200 accounts over Aug-Sep 2026, meaning roughly 12% of manual-read accounts were not completed in that window. This is a single-period snapshot with no pre-August baseline in the record, so it shows a shortfall but does not by itself establish that completion dropped since August.

E-05 still shows the field route-completion shortfall itself (88% vs 95% target, 9200 manual-read accounts, Aug-Sep 2026) as a standalone operational fact. It no longer supports that this shortfall is a genuine contributor to the ESTIMATED-dispute subset: E-12 shows those 1240 ESTIMATED bills are AMI-metered and dominated by import rejection, not manual-read route delays, contradicting PR-CHAIN-2's route-shortfall-to-estimate-substitution mechanism and partially contradicting PR-ROOT.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that no tariff change occurred this year corroborates the authoritative E-03 finding (billing-db.tariff_change_log returned zero records). As a non-authoritative stakeholder claim it adds no new evidence beyond what E-03 already established and does not resolve which process step is actually causing wrong bills.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative) claims the field reading crew has been three readers short since July, causing routes to run late and those customers to receive estimated bills. This offers a candidate causal mechanism for the route-completion shortfall already confirmed by E-05, but SH-FIELD has a stated incentive to secure contract headcount increases and a flagged bias toward staffing explanations, so the claim needs authoritative corroboration.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) authoritatively confirms the utility may request field route priority changes but they are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation, reinforcing the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval requirement for push_route_update. It is a governance/authority document and contributes nothing to identifying the billing dispute root cause.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) returns 14 routes each with its own completion value (sample route R-00 at 0.70), giving a per-route breakdown of the aggregate 88% shortfall already shown in E-05. The record contains only completion and route fields — no staffing/headcount data — so it cannot corroborate or refute SH-FIELD's staffing-shortage explanation (E-07/CL-03); it only confirms the shortfall is spread across many distinct routes.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-10 shows 320 accounts had an ESTIMATED read in the last billing cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes, but the record only carries account_id and route fields — no read_type/tariff/import-status breakdown. So it does not deliver the richer analysis (bills, read types, tariffs, import status) the pending work item intended, and cannot by itself confirm or refute the field-staffing or billing-defect causal mechanisms.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative) states that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today per vendor ticket TX-4471. This is only a stakeholder claim about access status, not AMI read-event data itself, so it does not yet speak to whether AMI read delivery contributed to disputes (U-AMI-CONTRIBUTION); it only suggests the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query may now be worth retrying.

The newly accessible mdms-export query (E-12) covers all 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (exactly matching E-04's ESTIMATED count) via AMI read_channel data: 1184 had an AMI read arrive before cutoff and get exported to billing but were rejected during import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 show true AMI non-delivery (NO_READ_RECEIVED). This indicates the entire ESTIMATED-dispute subset traces to AMI-metered accounts and is dominated by a billing-side import validation rejection rule, not by field-route delays or true AMI delivery failure.

U-DEFECT-MECHANISM.question: What specific billing import/validation rule or bill-issuance logic defect is producing incorrect bills across both ACTUAL and ESTIMATED reads?
U-DEFECT-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines what remediation is needed and whether any bill-write action can be authorized before the defect is located.
U-DEFECT-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule change log (DA-RULES) for changes around August and correlate with disputed ACTUAL-read bills.
U-DEFECT-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Keep disputed ACTUAL-read bills flagged for manual review; no automated bill corrections until the defect is located.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSE.question: Is the field route-completion shortfall actually caused by a 3-reader staffing gap since July as SH-FIELD claims, or by another factor?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSE.decision_impact: Affects whether remediation should target staffing/dispatch versus another route-completion cause; SH-FIELD has a stated incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias toward staffing explanations.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSE.resolution_path: Obtain authoritative ORG-FIELD staffing/roster records independent of SH-FIELD's statement.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the route-completion shortfall itself as confirmed but withhold any staffing-based remediation claim until corroborated.

U-AMI-CONTRIBUTION.question: Does an AMI/MDMS vendor read-delivery or validation issue contribute to any subset of the ESTIMATED-bill disputes, given mdms-export is currently inaccessible?
U-AMI-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: If AMI delivery problems exist, remediation scope would need to extend to ORG-AMI/vendor coordination rather than billing-side fixes alone.
U-AMI-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Provision vendor MDMS export access (currently ACCESS_PENDING per the recovery_decision HOLD log) and re-query read event data.
U-AMI-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Do not rule in or out AMI-side causes; limit current investigation and any remediation to billing-side and field-route pathways.
U-AMI-CONTRIBUTION.resolution: E-12 (authoritative, complete) shows AMI read_channel data covers all 1240 ESTIMATED-disputed bills: 1184 via billing-import REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (read arrived, billing rejected it) and 56 via true NO_READ_RECEIVED, so AMI vendor non-delivery contributes only a minor (4.5%) share, with the dominant mechanism being billing-side import rejection rather than an AMI/MDMS vendor fault.

U-HANDOFF-INTEGRITY.question: Are the H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL handoffs delivering and semantically valid, given both show UNKNOWN delivery_status and semantic_validity?
U-HANDOFF-INTEGRITY.decision_impact: Undetected handoff failures could be contributing to incorrect bills independent of the billing-side defect already identified.
U-HANDOFF-INTEGRITY.resolution_path: Audit handoff delivery logs and payload semantic checks for both channels.
U-HANDOFF-INTEGRITY.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-side defect investigation as the primary track while treating handoff integrity as an open secondary check.
